operators.name: custom_abs
semantics: Computes element-wise absolute value of input tensor x, equivalent to torch.abs(x).

The output tensor has the same shape, dtype, and device as the input, and must be contiguous or preserve the input strides? Reference torch.abs returns a new contiguous tensor with same strides if input is contiguous. For simplicity, output should be contiguous having same shape/dtype/device as input. The return tensor may be a copy with standard contiguous layout.
Supports arbitrary input strides by reading elements according to the provided strides; no assumption of row-major contiguity.
Element-wise absolute value of input tensor on CUDA, output same shape/dtype/device as input.
The input is float32 cuda tensor of shape [512, 3, 1024, 1024].
Since the size of dimension self.squeeze_axes (2) is 1024, not 1, squeeze is a no-op and returns the same tensor (or a view with identical data). The output shape remains [512, 3, 1024, 1024].
Returns the tensor after squeeze, identical to the abs result.
